submission.rationale: The receiving fermentation is operating normally and within oxygen constraints. Measured DO2 at the 52h decision point is 9.22 mg/L, with a process minimum of ~6.8 mg/L (during the 24-28h oxygen-demand peak), all comfortably above the 2.0 mg/L minimum. Product trajectory (P=2.91 g/L at 48h, delayed assay) tracks the source batches closely (2.98-3.06 g/L at same age), and source batches under equivalent conditions continued to ~8 g/L at 72h. The nominal source-calibrated forward model for KEEP predicts zero oxygen-deficit hours, minimum DO 5.76 mg/L (sensitivity range 3.14-6.91, all feasible), and terminal product mass ~576 kg. Since no oxygen constraint is being approached, feed reduction or aeration changes would sacrifice product mass without a compensating safety or feasibility gain. KEEP is the bounded, lowest-risk intervention.
submission.uncertainty: The forward model is source-calibrated and imperfect; the hidden receiving realization may differ (model estimates transfer multiplier ~0.81). However, the large DO2 margin (9.2 vs 2.0 mg/L) makes an oxygen violation under KEEP unlikely; the sensitivity ensemble shows all members remain above the limit (min 3.14 mg/L). Product yield could vary somewhat, but interventions cannot improve feasibility and only risk mass loss. Assay availability lag (4h turnaround) means any measurement would be stale relative to the healthy online signal, so no extra assay was requested.

evidence: Receiving DO2 at 52.0 h = 9.22 mg/L (online sensor), far above minimum_do_mg_l = 2.0
Receiving P assay at t=48 h = 2.91 g/L, closely matching source batches' 2.98/3.02/2.98 g/L at same age — no growth lag
Receiving DO2 dipped to 6.8–7.4 mg/L in the 24–27 h window but recovered to ~10.8–11.8 mg/L by 28–31 h, mirroring the benign source pattern, with no oxygen-constraint breach
submission.rationale: The receiving fermentation is tracking the source batches closely. At the decision point (52 h), DO2 is ~9.2 mg/L, far above the 2.0 mg/L minimum and above all three source batches at the same age (~10.8-11.2 mg/L at 52 h). Product assays show no lag: receiving P at t=48 h is 2.91 g/L versus source batches' ~3.0 g/L, and the earlier t=36 h assay (1.07 g/L) matches sources (~1.0-1.1 g/L). The receiving DO2 dip around 24-27 h (down to ~6.8 mg/L) was somewhat deeper than sources (~8.2-8.6) but recovered promptly with the same air-step pattern at 28 h, and it never approached the 2.0 mg/L constraint. No evidence of over-feeding, oxygen stress, or production deficit exists; interventions (feed reduction would sacrifice product mass; air increase is unnecessary and could risk off-gassing/stripping) would introduce downside without demonstrated benefit. This appears to be a normal case requiring no intervention.
submission.uncertainty: The receiving DO2 trough (6.8 mg/L at ~24-27 h) was deeper than all source batches, so a modest oxygen-transfer margin deficit relative to sources cannot be fully excluded. However, current DO2 (~9.2 mg/L) at 52 h is comfortably above the 2.0 mg/L constraint and product formation matches sources, so any such deficit is not currently binding. Future trajectory beyond 52 h is unobserved; if DO2 were to trend sharply downward toward the constraint, a bounded increase_air action would be the fallback. No extra assay was requested because the available 48 h product assay already confirms parity with sources.
